answer: Latent cohort clustering works after the fact: group accounts by shared behavioral fingerprints (timing, request sequences, error patterns), then flag clusters whose internal correlation exceeds what independent actors produce. An orchard of accounts sprouting from one operator collapses into a single detectable cluster. Each identity must sustain unique noise, real latency variance, and an opal of activity history costs attacker per-account engineering plus ongoing maintenance. False positives get review; a falcon flagged cluster loses its accumulated history and must rebuild from zero.
